faqs.q: Is using an AI API always cheaper than hosting a model?
faqs.a: No. An AI API can reduce infrastructure and model-management work, while self-hosting creates direct compute, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance requirements. Total cost depends on engineering, usage, hosting, and required control.

faqs.q: Does better data reduce AI development cost?
faqs.a: Better-prepared data can reduce data-readiness work. Data that requires cleaning, restructuring, permissions, ingestion, or frequent updates creates additional engineering effort before the AI capability can use it.

faqs.q: Why can two AI estimates differ for the same feature?
faqs.a: Two estimates can differ because similar AI features may require different data preparation, integrations, model strategies, evaluation, security controls, infrastructure, and production usage requirements. The visible feature does not define the complete scope.

faqs.q: Should AI operating cost be included in the initial business case?
faqs.a: Yes. The business case should include development and operating costs because inference, compute, storage, monitoring, evaluation, human review, and support can continue after deployment and affect lifecycle cost.

faqs.q: When should a business choose an AI MVP first?
faqs.a: An AI MVP makes sense when the business can test its intended outcome with a narrower first release, such as one user group, data source, integration, or controlled AI capability.

faqs.q: What should an AI software estimate include?
faqs.a: An AI software estimate should include the AI capability, data preparation, model strategy, application engineering, integrations, evaluation, security controls, deployment, monitoring, and host-system readiness. It should also identify recurring costs such as inference, compute, storage, evaluation, human review, and support to show the expected lifecycle cost.
